headline_marked: [[E Ink secondary display concept]] for phones offers always-on utility, better battery life
headline: E Ink secondary display concept for phones offers always-on utility, better battery life
summary: A Reddit user's concept replaces the Nothing Phone's Glyph Matrix with an E Ink display, promising superior battery life, sunlight readability, and distraction-free information at a glance.
details: A new concept envisions replacing the Nothing Phone's Glyph Matrix with an E Ink secondary display. This idea promises significant improvements over current micro-LED secondary screens, offering practical utility beyond a mere gimmick.

The E Ink display would provide an always-on screen that consumes minimal power, drastically extending battery life. It also boasts superior visibility in direct sunlight, making information easily readable outdoors.

Unlike the distracting full-color displays on modern flip phones or the limited functionality of Nothing's current Glyph Matrix, an E Ink screen focuses on delivering essential information without visual clutter. This could help reduce main screen distractions.

E-paper technology has advanced significantly, as seen in devices like the upcoming Pebble Round 2, which features complex colors and shapes with improved clarity. This demonstrates the viability of a sophisticated E Ink secondary display.

The concept, proposed by Reddit user Taweros, builds on previous community ideas but is more ambitious. It suggests a dedicated button, similar to Nothing phones, could switch between panels, integrating seamlessly.

This idea extends beyond Nothing phones, potentially offering a more functional alternative to rumored features like Pixel Glow on the upcoming Pixel 11. Utility, in this case, could be more compelling than flashy RGB lights.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI signs deal to show Getty's images]] in ChatGPT results and search
headline: OpenAI signs deal to show Getty's images in ChatGPT results and search
summary: Getty Images and OpenAI have formed a multi-year partnership to integrate Getty's licensed content into OpenAI's search and ChatGPT. This aims to enhance AI-powered search with high-quality, trustworthy visual content.
details: Getty Images and OpenAI have announced a multi-year partnership, bringing Getty's extensive licensed content libraries to the AI company. This agreement means Getty's high-quality visual content will now appear in OpenAI search and ChatGPT.
Getty CEO Craig Peters stated that licensed content makes AI-powered search and discovery more useful and trustworthy. The collaboration aims to deliver richer visual experiences to ChatGPT users.
A year prior, Getty launched its own generative AI tool, trained on its library and powered by NVIDIA's Edigy AI model. Images produced by this tool come with a royalty-free license.

It remains unconfirmed whether images from this new deal will be used for AI training, a detail not specified by Getty. This contrasts with their previous deal with Perplexity, where AI training use was explicitly disallowed.
caption:
